description: An isomorphic keyboard and pattern recorder played from a grid controller, with three stored control voltages and a pitch output

params.text: Sets the voltage on the control output beside it, 0V to 10V; a shape memory gesture on the grid recalls a stored value in its place
Short-press to open the preset view on the grid; press and hold to save the current state into the active preset slot
Click to reclaim a grid that has been taken by another module; the right-click menu is where a grid is first chosen

outputs.text: One of three control outputs, 0V to 10V, set by the knob beside it or recalled by a shape memory gesture on the grid
A pitch voltage for the note being played, 0V to 10V, following the position of the key in the grid's keymap
An 8V gate at each note event, whether the note came from playing the grid or from a pattern playing back

notes: this module produces nothing until a grid is connected. Add a grid 64, grid 128 or grid 256 module, or attach a hardware grid, then pick it from the Device Connection list.
once a pattern has been recorded from the grid, the grid can be disconnected and the pattern keeps playing.
a hardware grid needs serialosc installed; a virtual grid module needs nothing.
menu: Firmware Tools — opens a submenu naming the firmware and its version, with the input and output rate settings, a screenshot command, and the firmware reload commands
Input rate — sets how often the module reads its jacks, from 1x at the audio sample rate down to /16; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Output rate — sets how often the module writes its jacks, from 1x at the audio sample rate down to /16; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Save PNG screenshot — writes a picture of the module to disk; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Switch Firmware — loads a different firmware build into the module; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Hot Reload — reloads the firmware and keeps both the working memory and the stored presets; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Reload & Restart — reloads the firmware, discards the working memory and keeps the stored presets; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Clear NVRAM — wipes the module's stored presets and keeps the working memory; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Device Connection — lists the hardware and virtual grids the module can attach to; pick one to connect it, and the USB jack on the panel then shows a plug in it

outputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
